name: Allocation of Resources Without Limits or Throttling
principle: Code allocates reusable resources for an actor without enforcing maximum size, count, rate, or quota. Attackers can force CPU, memory, file, socket, process, thread, or disk exhaustion and deny service to other users.
detection_signals: C/C++ malloc(size), calloc(n,size), realloc(ptr,size), new[] or std::vector::resize(size) where size comes from request/input and has no upper-bound check
Java new byte[n], new Object[n], ByteBuffer.allocate(n), ArrayList(initialCapacity), StringBuilder(capacity) where n/capacity is request-controlled and not capped
accept(), ServerSocket.accept(), or socket handler loop creates fork(), pthread_create(), std::thread, new Thread(), or Executor task without max connection/thread/request limit
while/read loop writes request data to file, buffer, collection, or database until EOF with no byte counter or maximum total size
unbounded queue/map/list growth using add(), put(), push_back(), emplace(), offer(), or cache insert keyed by user input without eviction/quota
retry/poll/request processing loop lacks rate limiting, token bucket, semaphore, backpressure, or per-user/per-IP quota
open(), fopen(), socket(), epoll_create(), CreateFile-like handle allocation in request path without descriptor/handle count limit
negative_signals: input-controlled allocation size is checked against a fixed MAX_* constant before allocation
request loop increments totalBytes/items/connections and rejects or breaks when total exceeds a configured limit
resource acquisition is guarded by Semaphore, bounded ExecutorService/ThreadPoolExecutor, bounded queue, or connection pool with max size
per-user, per-IP, or authenticated-principal quota/rate limiter is enforced server-side before allocation
OS/environment resource limits are set and checked, such as setrlimit()/getrlimit(), cgroups, container memory limits, or JVM -Xmx plus application-level handling
allocation failure paths check NULL, std::bad_alloc, IOException, RejectedExecutionException, or offer() failure and fail closed
false_defense_traps: client-side size or rate checks without duplicate server-side enforcement
checking only size > 0 but not size <= MAX
authentication alone without per-principal quota or throttling
blacklisting suspicious values instead of allowlisting bounded ranges
global throttling only, allowing one attacker to degrade all valid users
verification_focus: Can an untrusted actor control the number, rate, or size of resource allocations without a server-side enforced maximum or throttle?

consequence_chains.trigger: Unvalidated input supplies allocation size, object count, loop count, or upload length
consequence_chains.consequence: Memory, disk, CPU, handle, thread, or process exhaustion causing denial of service

consequence_chains.trigger: Repeated or oversized allocations exceed available resources
consequence_chains.consequence: Uncontrolled resource consumption and service unavailability

consequence_chains.trigger: Single request-controlled size is passed to memory allocation without a maximum
consequence_chains.consequence: Excessive memory allocation causing process or system denial of service

patch_principle: Define explicit maximums for allocation size, object count, request rate, connection count, upload size, and protocol scale.
Enforce quotas and throttles server-side per user, tenant, IP, session, or privilege level before allocating resources.
Use bounded pools, bounded queues, semaphores, rate limiters, cache eviction, and OS/container resource limits.
Validate input with allowlisted numeric ranges and reject values outside configured limits.
Handle allocation failure safely and fail closed without cascading resource leaks.

minimal_examples.safe: if (request_len <= MAX_REQUEST) char *buf = malloc(request_len); else reject();
